tickets.title: Proposal to close Third Avenue L stop
tickets.summary: Joshua Walk, a software engineer, presented a simulation of 700 million MTA trips. It indicates closing the Third Avenue L stop would save riders about 1,800 hours a day. He noted the stop is not a transfer station or wheelchair accessible, and asked for two things: that it be referred to the transportation committee, and that the board consider piloting the closure with the MTA. Action: Refer the proposal to the transportation committee and decide whether to raise a pilot closure with the MTA.

tickets.title: 11th Street e-bike storage and delivery workers
tickets.summary: Over 100 e-bikes used by food delivery workers are stored on the block around the clock, obstructing the street and sidewalk, causing garbage problems, and driving out businesses and tenants. The 9th Precinct plans an enforcement action and bike confiscation starting October 7th. Advocacy groups asked instead for bikes to be tagged for two weeks, and signs are only in English, so multilingual and verbal outreach is needed. The district manager has worked on this since February 2024 and is searching for a fenced site and a better long-term solution. Action: District office to continue working with the precinct, elected officials, and worker groups on notice and outreach before October 7th, and keep seeking a legal storage site.

tickets.title: Indoor roller skating rink on East River pier
tickets.location_raw: East River Pier across from the Katherine Slip Mall
tickets.summary: A speaker pitched a 300,000 square foot, three-story multi-use building with an indoor roller skating rink on an East River pier. She said it would have $8 admission and create 250 to 500 local jobs, citing the closure of historic NYC rinks. Action: Refer the proposal to the land use committee for review.

tickets.title: Communication access and basic needs for deaf residents
tickets.summary: Vincent Jenkins spoke about NYCHA housing struggles, lack of food, water, and necessities, and the need for work. He also asked for communication access for deaf and hard of hearing people. He wants drugs and toxicity out of the community. Action: District office to follow up with Vincent Jenkins on NYCHA and communication access concerns.

tickets.title: Drug activity and dark areas in Seward Park
tickets.summary: Members of the public and the Seward Park Conservancy and Lower East Side Ecology Center report increased drug use and needles in Seward Park, with drug activity shifting from FDR Park to Seward and Tompkins Square Parks. Police presence, outreach, and harm reduction exist, but the district manager says a policy beyond moving activity around is needed. Board members also raised dark spots and unlit areas in the park and asked about mobile crisis teams. Action: District office to follow up with the precinct and Parks, collect reports of lights that are out from members who call 311, and explore non-police responses.

tickets.title: Transit costs for Immigrant Welcome Center access
tickets.summary: The Borough President's office opened the Manhattan Immigrant Welcome Center in northern Manhattan. Members asked about downtown organizations partnering with it and about offsetting transportation costs to reach it, since travel can take 60 minutes with transfers. The liaison said he would raise the cost question with the office. Action: Borough President's office to respond on transportation cost support, and downtown groups to contact the community liaison about partnerships.

tickets.title: Free public restroom pilot locations and access
tickets.summary: The city is installing free pilot public restrooms, with two in the district at Delancey and Suffolk and at Cooper Square at East Sixth Street and Third Avenue. DOT leads, installation is mid-October, and the pilot runs one year with a contractor cleaning them. The mayor's office asked for suggestions of nonprofit partners and locations for tap cards, and the committee raised concerns about access and emergency calls. Action: Transportation committee to bring a resolution next month on access and the pilot period, and members to send location suggestions to the mayor's office.

tickets.title: Seat new board member and assign mentor
tickets.summary: The chair welcomed newest board member Leila Mahia. A mentor will be assigned in the near future. Action: Board leadership to assign a mentor to Leila Mahia.

tickets.title: Second vice chair election
tickets.summary: Daniel Tano and Zachary Thomas ran for second vice chair, gave speeches, and the board voted by paper ballot. Daniel Tano won, 25 votes to 14. Action: Record the election result and seat Daniel Tano as second vice chair.

tickets.title: Board trainings on SLA, Robert's Rules, procedures
tickets.summary: The chair announced trainings for SLA matters, Robert's Rules, and office procedures, useful for new members and as a refresher for others. Dates and times are not yet set, and members may email topic requests. Action: Chair to schedule the trainings, report out dates and times, and collect training requests by email.

tickets.title: District needs statement and budget priorities vote
tickets.summary: In October the board will vote on its district needs and ranked expense and capital budget priorities for each agency. Committees do the work through the year, and every committee except SLA votes. Priorities favor programs needing funding, such as summer youth employment, over the most popular ones. Action: Committees to finalize ranked expense and capital priorities for each agency for the October vote.

tickets.title: City draft housing plan comments
tickets.summary: The board commented on the city's draft housing plan with little turnaround time, relying on the district needs statement. The plan calls for about 7,000 units in five years, 75% market rate, which does not meet the board's highest need of affordable housing. Members asked about ongoing input and were told committees must take positions proactively because notice periods are shrinking. Action: Land use committee to take positions proactively on future housing plans.

tickets.title: Correct August SLA resolutions numbers three and ten
tickets.summary: Two August SLA resolutions contained clerical errors. Number 10, Soft Hours Tea House, and number 3, Cozy Cafe, should recommend denial of a beer and wine license unless the applicant agrees to the stipulations, not a full on-premises license. Action: Correct both resolutions to read beer and wine license before sending to the SLA.

tickets.title: Denial of Allen Street liquor license application
tickets.summary: The board voted 20 to 10 with 9 abstentions to deny a full liquor license for item five on the August agenda, 11 Allen Street, an unlicensed location. The operator previously ran Time Cafe at Forsyth and Canal, which neighbors say has not kept its stipulations. The committee had negotiated stipulations, and the denial removes them, so the SLA could approve without conditions unless residents attend the SLA hearing. Action: Staff to add context about Time Cafe complaints to the resolution, organize residents to testify at the SLA, and share the SLA calendar date.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP postponement and resolutions
tickets.summary: The land use and economic development committees met EDC on the Essex Market RFP, due to be issued by the end of the month. EDC could not say what was incorporated from the board's two resolutions on keeping it a community market. The board asked EDC to postpone issuance. Action: Land use chair, the district manager, and an EDC contact will meet later this week to clarify, then update the full board.

tickets.title: Transportation equity analysis priorities
tickets.summary: The committee and district manager met the Independent Budget Office to analyze whether CB3 gets the transportation it needs compared to other districts. Three research ideas were selected, including cross-town buses and neighborhood parking locations. Action: Continue the equity analysis with IBO on the three chosen topics and report back.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge safety and Canal Street update
tickets.summary: The committee sent the mayor and DOT a letter restating the board's concerns about the foot of the Manhattan Bridge exits after a recent fatal crash. The letter also requested an update on the Canal Street redesign, which has had none since January. Action: Follow up with the mayor's office and DOT for a response and a Canal Street redesign update.

tickets.title: Request congestion pricing impact report
tickets.summary: A member asked whether MTA or DOT will return to report on congestion pricing effects, given the board's prior resolution about possible increased FDR congestion and the released air quality report. The committee chair said this could be followed up. Action: Transportation committee to ask MTA and DOT for reporting on congestion pricing impacts.

tickets.title: East River Park construction delay and ESCR updates
tickets.summary: The ESCR and BMCR team will return in October with limited detail on the BMCR work. Part of the East River Park construction is delayed, specifically the new facility for the Lower East Side Ecology Center and stewardship headquarters, due to procurement challenges. The team will report on the delays and address requests for better interim park stewardship support. Action: Parks committee to have the team return in October with details on the delays and stewardship support.

tickets.title: Mobile voting for education council elections
tickets.summary: The Health and Human Services committee presented a resolution urging NYC Public Schools to pilot mobile voting for Community and Citywide Education Council elections, where turnout is about 2%. Members asked that outreach be multilingual and make clear that immigration status is not collected and that the vote concerns school participation. Action: Full board to vote on the resolution and send it to NYC Public Schools, and relay the outreach concerns to the advocacy group.

tickets.title: Bylaws amendments on attendance procedures
tickets.summary: The bylaws task force proposed three changes. A new attendance process would have members with too many absences in six months meet with the executive committee. Attendance would be removed from the main removal process. Public members would be explicitly bound by the conflict of interest policies. A member noted the first edit reads as a double recommendation. Action: Email the proposed changes with the required 28-day notice and vote at the October full board meeting.
